undetermined_behaviors: Entry ordering: format.md never states the order in which entries are emitted. Probe {"b_key":"2","a_key":"1","c_key":"3"} is not in sorted key order, so insertion order and sorted order give different output. I chose the dict's own iteration order (insertion order).

Treatment of literal backslashes in a value: format.md only mandates escaping the characters ';' and '=', and is silent about backslash. Probes {"back":"\\"}, {"path":"C:\\tmp\\data",...}, and {"msg":"escape \\; literally",...} contain literal backslashes. A reader could reasonably escape backslashes too (for round-trippability), producing e.g. 'back=\\'; I implemented the literal spec and leave backslashes untouched, so a single backslash is emitted verbatim and 'escape \; literally' becomes 'escape \\; literally' (an ambiguous sequence on any hypothetical decode).
notes: format.md defines four rules: entries rendered as key=value, joined by ';', and the value-only escaping of ';' and '=' by a preceding backslash. I implemented exactly these and nothing more. Escaping is applied only to values, not keys (no probe key contains ';' or '='). The two gaps above are the only behaviors probes exercise that the text does not uniquely determine; empty values (probe {"single":""}) are determined -> 'single='.
